title: Electron install fails on glibc < 2.33 due to `@electron-internal/extract-zip`
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.4.1 and other versions using `@electron-internal/extract-zip`

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Debian 11 Bullseye

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

`install-electron` should install electron binaries on Linux distributions that are still supported.

### Actual Behavior

`install-electron` fails.

We build our Electron app on amd64 `node-24-bullseye` Docker image, which ships with glibc 2.31.

The recently added dependency `@electron-internal/extract-zip` raises the glibc requirement to 2.33. That seems unintended, because it excludes still-supported Linux distributions with older glibc versions, like the mentioned Debian 11.
